entities.evidence: The genealogy gives the age of the son Lamech named Noah in Genesis 5:29.
The second clause names the same Noah as the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Shem is the first son named as an object of “fathered,” alongside his brothers Ham and Japheth.
Noah fathers Ham, the son listed between Shem and Japheth.
Japheth is the third son named in the list of sons Noah fathered.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי links the subject נֹחַ to the age expression בֶּן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, stating that Noah was five hundred years old.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־, agreeing with נֹחַ.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי נֹחַ בֶּן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, the marked נֹחַ names the man who was five hundred years old. The genealogy continues the account of Lamech’s son named in Genesis 5:29.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בֶּן stands in construct before חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה ‘five hundred years’. The phrase gives Noah’s age: he was five hundred years old.
analysis.sense: one marked by an age, a quality or a fate (idiom)

analysis.evidence: חֲמֵשׁ counts מֵאוֹת ‘hundreds’. The phrase בֶּן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives Noah’s age as five hundred years.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute cardinal numeral, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה, חֲמֵשׁ counts five hundreds and שָׁנָה supplies the unit of time. Noah is five hundred years old.
analysis.morphology: Cardinal numeral, plural absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: hundreds (plural מֵאוֹת, with the digits: three hundred to nine hundred)

analysis.evidence: בֶּן חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה gives Noah’s age as five hundred years. The singular שָׁנָה supplies the unit counted.
Noah is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד. The repeated direct-object marker אֶת introduces Shem, Ham, and Japheth as the three sons he fathered.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ, the marked נֹחַ is the subject of “fathered.” It repeats the name from the first clause and identifies Noah as the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ אֶת שֵׁם, Noah is the subject of וַיּוֹלֶד ‘fathered’, and אֶת marks the personal name שֵׁם ‘Shem’ as its direct object. The marker recurs before Ham and Japheth in the same list.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ, “Noah fathered,” אֶת marks each son in turn. שֵׁם names the first son listed, followed by חָם and יָפֶת.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked אֶת introduces חָם (Ham), the second of the three sons named as direct objects of וַיּוֹלֶד (he fathered). Each name has its own object marker.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Clarify the existing Genesis 9:18 evidence note by identifying Ham’s place in the list at the first occurrence.
draft.definition: Ham, son of Noah and father of Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan.
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:18 first names Ham among Noah’s sons and then identifies him as Canaan’s father.

analysis.evidence: After וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ (“Noah fathered”), אֶת marks each son’s name as a direct object. חָם names the second son listed, between Shem and Japheth.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Ham, son of Noah and father of Canaan

draft.change: Add Gen.5.32 as an example of the existing definite-object sense in the article et.
draft.definition: Introduces a definite direct object, here a personal name in a series governed by one verb.
draft.evidence: In Gen.5.32, Noah fathered Shem, Ham, and Japheth. The repeated אֶת marks each name as an object of וַיּוֹלֶד.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת שֵׁם אֶת חָם וְאֶת יָפֶת, each son’s name has its own object marker. The marked אֶת introduces Japheth as the third object of וַיּוֹלֶד “he fathered”, and its prefix וְ־ joins him to the list.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed coordinating conjunction וְ־ “and” + unsuffixed direct-object particle אֶת.

analysis.evidence: After וַיּוֹלֶד נֹחַ ‘Noah fathered’, the repeated object marker אֶת introduces each son's name. The final phrase וְאֶת יָפֶת means ‘and Japheth’. At verse end, יָפֶת is the pausal form of יֶפֶת.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in pausal form, without prefix or suffix.
